problem:
The rate at which the number of particles in a radioactive substance decays $N(t),$ after $t$ years, can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}N}{\text{d}t}=-0.01N.
$$

How many years will it take for the number of particles to be $1%$ of the original number? Round your answer to the nearest year.

feedback.problem:
The amount of charge stored in a battery is decreasing due to self-discharge. The rate at which the amount of stored charge decays $W(t),$ after $t$ months, can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}W}{\text{d}t}=-0.025W.
$$

How long does it take for the amount of stored charge to be $75%$ of the original amount? Round your answer to the nearest month.
feedback.worked_solution:
We model the amount of stored charge using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}W}{\text{d}t}=-0.025W.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
W(t)={W}_{0}\,{e}^{-0.025t},
$$

where ${W}_{0}$ is the initial stored charge.

Let ${t}_{1}$ be the time when the amount of stored charge is $75%$ of the original amount. That is,

$$
W({t}_{1})=0.75{W}_{0}.
$$

We solve the above equation for ${t}_{1},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}0.75{W}_{0} & ={W}_{0}\,{e}^{-0.025{t}_{1}} \\ 0.75 & ={e}^{-0.025{t}_{1}} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.75) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-0.025{t}_{1}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.75) & =-0.025{t}_{1} \\ {t}_{1} & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.75)}{0.025} \\ {t}_{1} & ≈11.507\end{aligned}
$$

Rounding to the nearest month, we conclude that it takes $12$ months for the amount of stored charge to be $75%$ of the original amount.
